conflicts.description: The Threadwrights and Emberwrights blame each other for the failing keystones, each withholding their craft and fueling a standoff that accelerates the decay.
conflicts.name: Thread and Stone

conflicts.description: The Starwardens insist the drift is destined and oppose the Cartographers' Circle, whose maps prove the bridges can be saved if the isles cooperate.
conflicts.name: Prophecy Versus Charts

description: The Aurelian Drift is a fractured realm of four great floating islands, each adrift in a sea of luminous cloud and held in a fragile orbit by the ancient skybridges, woven spans of starlit stone and living silverthread that carry travelers, trade, and the tides of magic from isle to isle. Once a single unified continent, the realm was sundered long ago, and only the skybridges have kept the archipelago from drifting apart. This is a high fantasy of wonder and discovery for young readers: sunrise glows along crystal cliffs, windwhales sing through the cloud-valleys, and every island speaks its own dialect of myth. But the bridges are now failing, their silverthread fraying and their runes going dim, while the rival enclaves who tend them have grown suspicious and isolated. A young cartographer, whose maps reveal the pattern of the decay, must persuade the enclaves to set aside old grudges and rekindle the bridges before the islands drift beyond each other's reach.

factions.description: Mapmakers and wayfinders of Lumenvale who record the realm's shifting geography and hold the only complete charts of the skybridge network.
factions.name: The Cartographers' Circle

factions.description: Astronomer-priests of Ostrelune who believe the bridges are guided by the stars and that the drift is a prophecy to be accepted, not resisted.
factions.name: The Starwardens

factions.description: Guild of Vellamar weavers who control the supply of silverthread and use it as leverage in trade with the other isles.
factions.name: The Threadwrights

factions.description: Smith-clans of Cindrelle who forge the rune-stones of the skybridges and keep their secret techniques from outsiders.
factions.name: The Emberwrights

history.description: The original continent shattered and rose into the sky, leaving four islands adrift until the first skybridge, the Heartspan, was raised to bind them.
history.name: The Sundering

history.description: The Threadwrights and Emberwrights swore to join silverthread and rune-stone in every keystone, founding the shared craft of the bridges.
history.name: The Threadpact

history.description: After a dispute over a stolen chart, Lumenvale sealed its map archive to outsiders, sowing distrust among the isles.
history.name: The Closing of the Archive

history.description: The southern bridge between Cindrelle and Vellamar cracked and dimmed, the earliest sign of the failure that now threatens the realm.
history.name: The First Fraying

locations.description: The central island, crowned with terraced gardens and a bell-tower archive of maps. It anchors the oldest skybridge, the Heartspan, and is home to the cartographers' guild.
locations.name: Lumenvale

locations.description: A pale island of silver orchards and moonlit observatories to the north, where scholars read the stars and measure the drift of the isles with delicate instruments of glass and brass.
locations.name: Ostrelune

locations.description: A windswept eastern island of ropewalks, sail-workshops, and harbors for cloud-ships. Its weavers spin the silverthread that sustains every skybridge, though their stores are running low.
locations.name: Vellamar

locations.description: A warm southern island of glowing amber caverns and forges heated by volcanic vents. Its smiths carve the rune-stones set into each skybridge, and they guard their craft jealously.
locations.name: Cindrelle

name: The Aurelian Drift

rules.statement: Each island floats because of a lattice of skystone beneath it, and the lattice weakens when its skybridge anchors lose resonance.
A skybridge only holds while a rune-stone from one isle and silverthread from another are joined in its keystone, so no single enclave can sustain a bridge alone.
Cloud tides rise and fall with the seasons, shifting the distance between islands by up to a league.
By ancient custom, any traveler crossing a skybridge is granted hospitality by the enclave on the far side for three days.
Technology of the realm relies on wind, glass, brass, and woven thread; cloud-ships are driven by sails and sky-currents rather than engines of fire.
